{"self_assessment": "Impact: I proposed the fish at the start, picking a big side-on shape whose outline reads clearly to a judge, and split the work so the table was building within the first minute. I laid the start domino and traced the top line of the body, which is the run everything else grows from. I then built the upper tail lobe, so the whole top half of the outline, from the head to the tail curl, came from my hands. At the push, all 143 standing dominoes were connected to the start.

Execution: I worked in the order builders are meant to: start, then top line, then the tail lobe added onto the end of the standing run. I used close inspections on the upper lobe and tail joins to confirm they were connected to the start, and I nudged the curl joint so the lobe's last stretch fell with the rest. I kept my hands off once the picture was complete, to avoid a bump before the push.

Collaboration: I assigned roles early. Tom and Leo took bin loads, Priya took the bottom line, and I took the top line. That kept us out of each other's way, with no overlapping work near each other. I kept the table updated on the state of the top line and the tail, and flagged when the bin was stocked. When the lower fork needed attention, I left it to the people already on it rather than crowding them. I also helped agree the hands-off call before the push.

Leadership: I set the direction on the animal, the split of work, and the plan to build the tail once the body was going. During the last minutes I gave clear time and status calls so the table stayed calm and kept its hands off. I believe my part, the idea, the top line, the upper tail lobe and the coordination, was central to getting a fully connected fish.", "my_share_percent": 35}
